title: What’s good about ai trading?
author: neural_candy
selftext:
What’s really good thing about ai trading? It’s obviously not giving you a free investment profit and actually it can be an auto money losing machine. Isn’t it?

I am very interested in it actually. Please enlighten me! 🙏

replies.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
replies.body: the bot won't revenge trade, but the person running it can still double its size after a loss or switch models after every bad week. I'd want the sizing and shutdown rules decided beforehand too

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the good part isn't the trades, it's how fast you can test an idea now: describe a rule, get it coded and backtested in an evening. the money losing machine shows up when people skip the test and let it trade straight away. Quantradin, something I built, does that loop on paper: rule in your own words, graded without peeking ahead. quantradin.com

comments.author: Bergodrake
comments.body: Talking about ML, besides the automation part, the good thing is that with ML you have models that can pick good trades with a set of dynamic and sophisticated rules, rather than rely on simple "human readable" ones that continuously need to be adapted

comments.author: HaltingComplexity3
comments.body: AI sorts the noise while moon keeps the actual call human

comments.author: Squared_Nutz
comments.body:
Auto money printing machine, actually. Account has doubled in a month, and headed towards 4x'ing before November. All I do is check it twice a day (10 minutes), and make tweaks weekly (1-2 hours).

LLM's give you the advantage of testing multiple strategy ideas and pull data quickly, getting something up and running in DAYS... for what might have otherwise taken MONTHS of work- if you even know how to code in the first place. Get your strategies right using your choice of LLM, and don't be afraid to run them on real money for testing. 

Numbers hidden because some of these groups have PnL porn phobia. LOL

https://reddit.com/link/pf2ojql/video/p3npr4jw1ouh1/player

replies.author: Lopsided_Step3549
replies.body: Can you give example of one strategy? I am new to trading.

comments.author: ApartmentOk3498
comments.body: filtering noise and testing ideas faster, prospero is useful on the research and signals

comments.author: Key-Enthusiasm-3403
comments.body:
Honestly the real upside is speed. You can describe a rule in plain English and have it coded and tested in an evening, which used to take weeks. That part is genuinely good.



You're right about the other half though. Most of the "my AI doubled my account" stories never show a baseline. Doubling in a month in a market that went up is just being long. What I'd want to see is the same rule against doing nothing clever, a random entry with the same exit, over a few hundred trades.



Because an LLM will happily hand you a strategy that fits the last six months perfectly. Easy to build, easy to overfit, and it feels like an edge while you're testing it on data it's already seen.



So I'd say it's good for testing ideas fast and bad as a reason to trust one. I'm not sure it beats a simple rule you could write on a napkin, I haven't seen anyone show that properly.

comments.author: Upper-Worker8516
comments.body: It's can automate certain parts of research. But human must make final decision

comments.author: teckel
comments.body:
The agentic trading agent I wrote which is trading my real money (not a paper account) is up slightly more than the market. It's been running about 4 months, but even if it was just matching the market I'd say it's useful to my portfolio as it's using different trading strategies and trading some equities I'd typically never trade.

I even run a Discord channel that shows all the daily market research, trades, and daily account returns.

comments.author: chikeez
comments.body:
Rapid testing and strategy ideation/generation.  

If we’re talking about LLMs:
